headline: Oratomic, a Pasadena startup building quantum computers from arrays of atoms, has raised $475 million in a Series B round at a $5.4 billion valuation.
score_reason: Lowered from 7: the financing was announced on 8 Oct 2026, so the WSJ valuation report is a week old; only the local report was readable.
importance_line: Large private bets are flowing into neutral-atom quantum computing, but Oratomic has given no timetable for a working machine, and the error-correction method its team proposed in March is still theory, so the valuation rests on promise rather than a built computer.
summary: Pasadena Now reports, citing the law firm Wilson Sonsini Goodrich & Rosati, that Oratomic's Series B round, announced on 8 Oct 2026 and led by backers including ARCH Venture Partners, Spark Capital, Khosla Ventures, Index Ventures, General Catalyst and Bezos Expeditions, brings its total funding to $775 million since its March launch; the Wall Street Journal ran an exclusive on the valuation on 16 Oct 2026. The company says the money will pay for more scientists and engineers, laboratories and the systems needed to build its machines.
notes: WSJ article paywalled (401); read Pasadena Now. Underlying financing dates from 8 Oct 2026, so older news re-dated by the WSJ exclusive; score lowered by 2. WSJ headline not read in full.
